terra.problem: The Mount of Olives' location is a fact from outside the passage, but the explanation gives no supporting reference for it.
The text does not say the cords were lying around or that Jesus made the whip right there.
Saying nobody gets to stay behind goes beyond the text. Jesus and His disciples are also present in the account.
Saying the animals went out with everyone else goes beyond what the passage says. It names the sheep and cattle among those driven out.
The imagined afternoon of picking up coins adds a time and an event the text does not give.
The explanation is generic and ends with a vague observation rather than Papa Dorin's distinctive voice.
Calling the baker's answer a stretch puts down the answer rather than responding kindly.
The passage does not say that nobody in the courtyard is resting.
Saying three days sounds wild to the Jews states their reaction as fact, rather than marking it as Papa Dorin's impression.
The passage does not say the Jews thought three days was impossible or that the forty-six years was why they thought so.
The explanation is flat and generic, repeating the number and offering only a broad observation about building.
The cited verse supports Solomon's building of the temple, but it does not establish that he was David's son. That detail needs a supporting reference.
The text says when the disciples remembered Jesus' words, not that the words failed to click for them in the moment.
The explanation says Jesus did not need anyone to explain people to Him is in the cited verse, John 2:24. That detail comes from verse 25.
